title: i-DILI: A Multi Source Database for Drug Induced Liver Injury Labeling and Benchmarking
content: Drug-Induced Liver Injury (DILI) is liver damage caused by a drug or its metabolites. Machine learning models for DILI need clean labels and chemical structures for accurate DILI prediction. The currently avaialble Public DILI data is not constistent in terms of labelling. And on few occasions they contradict each other. Assay-only datasets are usually biased towards positive compounds. On the other hand Clinical datasets are smaller and implement different rules. We built i-DILI, a multi-source DILI database. The pipeline supports seven public resources: LiverTox, DILIrank, DILIst, SIDER, DrugBank, Open TG-GATEs, and Tox21. This build includes six of them; SIDER contributes zero rows because its files use compound IDs rather than drug names. Each compound receives a binary DILI label and a confidence score Cf that reflects how much we trust that label after sources agree or conflict. The database has 17,778 unique compounds 22.47% positive, 77.53% negative, mean Cf=0.603, and valid SMILES for 85.3% of compounds. To check that the labels are usable for modeling, we train fingerprint classifiers under 5-fold cross-validation and a scaffold split, including tree ensembles, a shallow MLP, and a deeper DNN. We also place published DILI models in context without claiming a head-to-head ranking. i-DILI is a data resource for DILI labeling and benchmarking, not a claim of best-in-class DILI prediction.
